findings.summary: 3D computer graphics use a three-dimensional geometric data representation to generate two-dimensional images through modeling, animation, and rendering. Models are constructed from polygonal meshes of vertices, and scenes are lit and animated before being rasterized. The workflow separates formation of shape, placement and motion, and final image generation via light transport simulation. Rendering techniques range from polygon shading to path tracing, with hardware acceleration enabling real-time display.

mechanisms.title: Polygonal Mesh Construction
mechanisms.explanation: 3D models are formed from vertices that define polygons, typically triangles. The integrity and suitability for animation depend on polygon structure. Meshes can originate from artist tools, 3D scanning, procedural generation, or physical simulation.

mechanisms.title: Rendering Light Transport
mechanisms.explanation: The rendering phase calculates how light travels from sources to the viewer, simulating transport and scattering across surfaces. Techniques include vertex illumination interpolation, ray tracing, distributed ray tracing, and path tracing, which approximate global effects such as reflection, refraction, and depth of field.
